progressionNote: Power costs, opposed pools, and numerical limits remain alpha playtest values. The six-family identity and rank-by-rank functions are canonical; exact balance may change after table testing.

diceSystem.complicationRule: A failed roll containing one or more 1s creates a Complication.

archetypes.name: Human Investigator
archetypes.theme: A mortal continuity specialist who survives by deciding what counts as evidence, responsibility, consent, and human conduct when every supporting institution has disappeared.
archetypes.weaknessText: You possess no automatic supernatural immunity. Severe harm, deprivation, fear, isolation, and the cumulative burden of being the team's evidentiary and moral reference point affect you normally.

innateAbilities.name: Prepared Contingency
innateAbilities.effect: Once per operation, establish one plausible precaution, item, credential, contact method, or escape provision prepared before the scene. It creates leverage but cannot solve the entire operation by itself.

innateAbilities.name: Evidence Chain
innateAbilities.effect: When you preserve and compare evidence from at least two scenes, gain one bonus die on the next Investigation, Negotiation, or Command test that directly exploits the connection.

innateAbilities.name: Hold the Human Line
innateAbilities.effect: Spend 1 Conviction to ignore one fear, coercion, identity-disruption, or dehumanizing classification penalty for a scene and name the principle you are refusing to surrender.

powerFamilies.name: Casecraft
powerFamilies.description: Casecraft begins as disciplined investigation and develops into the ability to reconstruct responsibility across copied minds, edited records, alien biology, autonomous systems, and events deliberately stripped of a single accountable witness.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Crime-scene procedure, witness examination, documentary research, forensic comparison, occult investigation, and the stubborn habit of asking who benefited.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: The printed body learns to interpret chemical residue, deck vibration, noospheric discontinuity, printer artifacts, and contradictory identity histories as evidence rather than noise.

abilities.name: Residual Read
abilities.effect: Cost: none. Test: Awareness + Investigation, difficulty 1-3. After examining a person, object, or location for one exchange, ask one concrete question about what interacted with it most recently, what was deliberately concealed, or which detail does not belong. The answer identifies usable evidence rather than solving motive. Failure: the strongest irrelevant pattern becomes temporarily persuasive until contradicted.

abilities.name: Contradiction Ledger
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction or ten minutes of uninterrupted work. Test: Reason + Investigation. Record two statements, logs, memories, or physical traces that cannot all be true. For the remainder of the operation, gain two dice when testing the contradiction, and the Game Moderator must indicate which missing assumption would allow both records to coexist. Failure: you correctly identify a contradiction but misidentify which source was altered.

abilities.name: Reconstruct the Event
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction. Test: Reason + Investigation, difficulty 3. Assemble a probable sequence from surviving residue, including one unseen transition between known facts. The reconstruction can reveal entry route, timing, likely number of actors, or the action an autonomous system attempted to omit. Failure: the sequence is useful but imports one detail from a fragmented personal memory.

abilities.name: Cross-Continuity Indictment
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction and one preserved piece of evidence. Test: Resolve + Investigation opposed by the target's Guile + Noospherics or equivalent. Establish that a person, copy, institution, machine process, or legal identity remains responsible despite body replacement, memory editing, subcontracting, or ownership transfer. Success removes two dice from attempts to deny, redirect, or procedurally erase that responsibility for the scene. Failure: the accusation exposes your evidence chain and gives the target a route to attack it.

abilities.name: The Case Will Break
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Conviction and 1 Strain. Name the central unanswered question of the current operation and summarize the evidence already earned. The Game Moderator must reveal a concrete, reachable route by which the truth can be proven, including the person, system, site, or risk that blocks it. This does not provide the answer or make the route safe. Failure is impossible, but the route always exposes a truth capable of changing the team's understanding of the mission.

powerFamilies.name: Field Discipline
powerFamilies.description: Field Discipline turns mortal training into a stabilizing combat doctrine. It does not imitate supernatural toughness; it makes preparation, movement, fire control, triage, and mutual protection reliable while everyone else's inherited instincts are malfunctioning.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Military procedure, protective operations, emergency response, practiced violence, controlled breathing, and the refusal to freeze when the impossible becomes immediate.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: Distributed reflex tissues and alien regulatory organs begin executing learned procedures before conscious thought finishes, creating extraordinary reliability at the cost of reflexes that may belong to another iteration.

abilities.name: Steady Hands
abilities.effect: Cost: none once per round. Ignore one die of injury, fear, recoil, environmental instability, or unfamiliar equipment penalty during a precise action. If the action protects another person, also prevent the first Complication created by environmental conditions. Failure: none, but repeated use while badly injured adds 1 Strain at scene end.

abilities.name: Controlled Advance
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction. Test: Awareness + Command or Firearms. Establish a safe movement interval through fire, collapsing terrain, hostile machinery, or panicked crowds. You and one ally may reposition without surrendering active defense, and anyone following the route gains one die. Failure: the route remains possible, but one concealed threat gains a free reaction.

abilities.name: No One Left Behind
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction. Reaction when an ally would be incapacitated, separated, vented, captured, or removed from the local noosphere. Move toward them immediately, stabilize their condition, or preserve a physical tether, signal, or identity lock long enough for another action. Failure: you preserve them but share one level of their damage, Exposure, or Archetype Pressure.

abilities.name: Kill-Box Literacy
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction. Test: Reason + Awareness at the start of a conflict. Identify the scene's true lines of fire, structural failure points, cover hierarchy, and escape geometry. For three rounds, allies who follow your calls gain one die to Guard, ranged attacks, or movement tests; enemies using the predicted routes lose one die. Failure: the model is accurate until the environment changes, at which point it becomes dangerously obsolete.

abilities.name: Mortal Defiance
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Conviction and 1 Strain. When confronting a being, system, or event that is clearly beyond ordinary human scale, declare the single action that must succeed for others to survive. Add Resolve to the relevant pool, ignore current fear and injury penalties, and remain active until the action resolves even if you would otherwise fall. Afterward, convert one suffered Impact into Trauma and record what the body permanently learned from surviving it.

powerFamilies.name: Continuity Anchoring
powerFamilies.description: Continuity Anchoring protects identity when memories, bodies, legal personhood, and noospheric records disagree. The Investigator becomes capable of holding a self or relationship steady without pretending uncertainty does not exist.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Personal testimony, therapeutic grounding, oath keeping, witness protection, moral conviction, and the social fact that people become real to one another through repeated recognition.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: The Investigator's broad printed biology begins broadcasting stable emotional, chemical, and noospheric reference patterns that other continuations can use to reassemble a coherent claim to self.

abilities.name: Name Yourself
abilities.effect: Cost: none once per scene. State your name, one chosen identity claim, and one memory you accept as yours. Remove one die of Disruption or identity-confusion penalty and prevent a minor external system from assigning you a contradictory role for the exchange. Failure: none, but the declared memory becomes a vulnerable anchor others can target.

abilities.name: Anchor Another
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction. Test: Empathy + Resolve opposed by the strength of the intrusion. Through touch, voice, or a shared token, remind an ally of a relationship, promise, or behavior that belongs to them. Suppress one compulsion, false memory, possession cue, or noospheric identity overwrite for a scene. Failure: the ally stabilizes but one of their intrusive impressions transfers to you.

abilities.name: Shared Baseline
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction per scene. Establish a small set of agreed facts for the team: who is present, what the immediate objective is, and what no member consents to surrender. Allies within communication range gain one die against fear, domination, memory editing, and conflicting sensor narratives. Failure: the baseline holds, but one stated fact later proves incomplete rather than false.

abilities.name: Refuse the Edit
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction and mark 1 Exposure. Reaction when a power, system, contract, or authority would erase, replace, merge, or legally invalidate a person. Test Resolve + Cohesion against the effect. On success, preserve an unaltered witness copy of the targeted identity inside your own memory and force the effect to leave a detectable seam. Failure: the edit proceeds, but you retain a painful and incomplete version of what was removed.

abilities.name: Human Standard
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Conviction and 1 Strain. For one scene, define a human-scale principle of personhood such as informed consent, continuity of responsibility, bodily autonomy, or the right of a copy to refuse reintegration. Allies who knowingly accept the standard may use your Resolve in place of their own lower Identity Defense, while systems attempting to violate it must overcome a difficulty equal to your Archetype Rating. The principle cannot compel agreement; it gives resistance to those who choose it.

powerFamilies.name: Institutional Ghostcraft
powerFamilies.description: Institutional Ghostcraft weaponizes the Investigator's understanding of organizations. In a future where personhood is authenticated by systems, the Investigator learns to read procedure, borrow legitimacy, and build temporary jurisdiction from the expectations institutions cannot stop having.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Bureaucratic literacy, credentials, chain of command, warrants, access policies, emergency authority, labor rules, and the ability to make institutions reveal what they value by watching what they require.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: The Investigator combines social performance with noospheric observation, creating temporary institutional roles that are convincing because they satisfy a system's own procedural assumptions.

abilities.name: Read the Hierarchy
abilities.effect: Cost: none. Test: Awareness + Xenoculture or Investigation. After observing an organization or automated facility, identify who can authorize exceptions, what resource actually controls behavior, and which rule is ceremonial rather than enforced. Failure: identify the formal hierarchy while missing the hidden dependency that truly governs it.

abilities.name: Borrowed Credentials
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction. Test: Guile + Security or Negotiation. Present yourself as a plausible inspector, contractor, emergency responder, inherited process, or provisional identity long enough to obtain one limited access privilege. Success lasts until directly audited or used outside the declared role. Failure: access is granted but flagged for delayed review.

abilities.name: Procedural Trap
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction and five minutes of preparation. Create a documentation, safety, jurisdictional, contractual, or chain-of-command contradiction that forces an institution to pause one hostile action until someone accepts explicit responsibility. Failure: the pause occurs, but the institution identifies you as the source of the conflict.

abilities.name: Manufacture Jurisdiction
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction and a credible public objective. Test: Presence + Command. Establish a temporary operational authority over a site, emergency, investigation, or evacuation. Neutral personnel and ordinary systems treat your instructions as presumptively valid for the scene unless a superior claimant defeats you in an opposed institutional or social test. Failure: you gain cooperation from individuals but no system-level recognition.

abilities.name: Found an Institution
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Conviction, 1 Strain, and a group willing to participate. Create a durable protocol, office, mutual-aid cell, investigative body, or emergency authority with a defined purpose and limits. It gains a recognizable noospheric identity, can issue narrow credentials, and survives your absence as long as members continue performing its function. This is not mind control; it is the creation of real social infrastructure where none existed.

powerFamilies.name: Contingency Engineering
powerFamilies.description: Contingency Engineering is the art of preserving options under impossible uncertainty. It turns foresight, salvage, routes, caches, and failure analysis into practical leverage without granting supernatural omniscience.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Operational planning, dead drops, equipment caches, escape routes, redundancy, disaster preparation, and the professional assumption that every plan will eventually fail.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: The printed body's heightened pattern recognition and the Investigator's fragmented memories combine into instinctive awareness of what will be needed, sometimes because another iteration already learned the lesson.

abilities.name: Pocket Solution
abilities.effect: Cost: none once per scene. Produce or improvise one small ordinary tool, adapter, restraint, seal, marker, charge, medical supply, or evidence container from carried gear and nearby salvage. It must be plausible and limited to one immediate function. Failure: the solution works once and then becomes unusable.

abilities.name: Route of Escape
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction. Test: Awareness + Survival or Security. Identify a concealed, neglected, hazardous, or socially invisible route out of the current area. The route is real but may require a sacrifice such as abandoning equipment, crossing hostile atmosphere, or exposing the team to observation. Failure: the route exists but closes after the first person uses it.

abilities.name: Cached Countermeasure
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction and one previously visited scene, allied contact, or accessible storage point. Establish that you prepared a narrow countermeasure against a known threat: filtered ammunition, a signal jammer, a ritual interruption kit, a metabolic suppressant, a false identity package, or similar provision. Failure: the cache exists but has degraded, been moved, or acquired an owner.

abilities.name: Operational Reversal
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction and one round spent observing failure. Test: Reason + Command. Convert a broken plan into a new objective that uses the enemy's preparation, the environment, or the mission's abandoned assumptions. Allies who accept the reversal may immediately reposition or change targets and gain one die on the first action supporting it. Failure: the reversal creates an opening but sacrifices one secondary objective.

abilities.name: Everything Has a Failure Mode
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Conviction and 1 Strain. After studying a supernatural power, institution, machine, organism, or security system, declare the specific condition under which it can be interrupted, bypassed, overloaded, embarrassed, or forced to choose between incompatible priorities. The Game Moderator defines the required setup and consequence. The weakness is never effortless, but it is real and repeatable until the target fundamentally changes.

powerFamilies.name: Human Network
powerFamilies.description: Human Network treats trust, testimony, mutual obligation, and shared competence as strategic assets. It is the Investigator's answer to a universe where Charles can no longer materialize support and identity systems cannot replace actual relationships.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Contacts, informants, community ties, witness care, teamwork, reputation, favors, and the recognition that institutions function only because particular people continue doing the work.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: Repeated recognition between continuations creates stable social and noospheric pathways that can survive body changes, false records, and the absence of formal legal status.

abilities.name: Earned Trust
abilities.effect: Cost: none once per scene. After you materially help, protect, or tell a difficult truth to someone, mark them as a provisional contact. Gain one die on later good-faith social tests with them, and they can recognize you through one superficial disguise or identity inconsistency. Failure: trust is possible, but they require proof you cannot immediately provide.

abilities.name: Witness Protection
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction. Designate a frightened, hunted, or socially vulnerable person under your protection. For the scene, you can intercept one attempt to coerce, erase, isolate, or discredit them, and they gain one die to remember or testify accurately while you remain present. Failure: you preserve their testimony but reveal your involvement.

abilities.name: Cell of Competence
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction and three willing participants. Assign each participant a practical responsibility and establish a simple communication procedure. While the cell follows the plan, members may lend one Skill die to another member once per round without acting themselves. Failure: the cell functions, but one unassigned problem becomes the source of a Complication.

abilities.name: Mutual Obligation
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Conviction and a favor genuinely owed or offered. Formalize a reciprocal commitment between individuals, copies, or organizations without supernatural compulsion. Each side gains two dice when honoring the exact commitment and suffers one Strain, Feedback, Hunger, Intrusion, Discord, or equivalent pressure if they knowingly betray it. Failure: the obligation remains social rather than mechanically reinforced.

abilities.name: Civilization Is People
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Conviction and sustained work across at least one operation. Convert a scattered group of survivors, contacts, workers, copies, or local intelligences into a functioning support community with agreed protections, shared resources, and procedures for resolving internal conflict. The community becomes a persistent campaign asset capable of shelter, information, logistics, or political pressure. Its loyalty depends on how it is treated, not on your power rating.

archetypes.name: Vampire
archetypes.theme: A dead self-pattern reconstructed as a living alien organism, forced to decide whether undeath is a metaphysical fact, a bloodline identity, or a predatory instruction the new body is learning to obey.
archetypes.weaknessText: Direct unfiltered stellar radiation causes severe harm, but different spectra produce uncertain reactions. Hunger rises when nourishment, Vitae, and predatory satisfaction fall out of alignment.

innateAbilities.name: Predator's Blood
innateAbilities.effect: Spend 1 Vitae to add Archetype Rating to one Force, Finesse, Resilience, Presence, or Guile test as catalytic fluid forces the living printed body to obey an inherited death-command.

innateAbilities.name: Deathless Body
innateAbilities.effect: You resist poison, disease, ordinary aging, suffocation, and vacuum exposure through metabolic suspension and nonhuman repair. Fire, intense radiation, and catastrophic tissue loss remain especially dangerous.

innateAbilities.name: Feeding
innateAbilities.effect: Blood or compatible vital media can restore Vitae, but not every source quiets Hunger. Alien nourishment may carry sensory contamination, mutation, memory fragments, or ethical consequences.

powerFamilies.name: Crimson Velocity
powerFamilies.description: Crimson Velocity converts Vitae into overlapping motor intervals. It begins as speed and develops into a localized disagreement between the Vampire's movement and the sequence in which the surrounding world records it.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Blood forced dead muscle, sharpened reflexes, and predatory acceleration beyond mortal reaction time.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: Catalytic fluid floods distributed nerve clusters and elastic internal plates, allowing several motor decisions to begin before earlier ones have fully completed.

abilities.name: Quickened Step
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Vitae. Add two dice to Initiative, pursuit, sudden movement, or an attempt to reach cover before a hazard resolves. Your body preloads the route through distributed nerves. Failure: you still move, but one limb or reflex completes an outdated instruction and creates a minor positional Complication.

abilities.name: Blurred Passage
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Vitae. Test: Finesse + Athletics opposed by Awareness. Cross a nearby exposed space, pass a closing barrier, or move between two observers before ordinary reactions can coordinate. Cameras record an incomplete sequence rather than true invisibility. Failure: you arrive, but the route leaves a clear thermal or biological trace.

abilities.name: Second Motion
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Vitae and gain 1 Hunger if used twice in a scene. Perform a second minor action or movement after your primary action, provided it follows the same immediate objective. You may draw and fire, move and seal a hatch, or strike and withdraw. Failure: the second motion occurs, but you lose active defense until your next turn.

abilities.name: Red Interval
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Vitae. For one round, choose a target or hazard. Your actions against it are resolved as though you began moving a fraction of a second before the decision became visible; its active defenses lose two dice and you may interrupt one ordinary reaction. Failure: the interval opens, but your senses desynchronize and impose two dice of penalty on your next nonphysical action.

abilities.name: Moment of Slaughter
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Vitae and 1 Hunger. Take one complete turn before normal Initiative, then take your normal turn later with one fewer action. During the first turn, local sensors may record your attacks, movement, and impacts in the wrong order. Failure is not rolled, but afterward the body continues consuming Vitae until you feed, enter dormancy, or accept 1 Trauma from metabolic collapse.

powerFamilies.name: Grave Dominion
powerFamilies.description: Grave Dominion is predatory authority translated into chemistry, posture, voice, attention, and noospheric priority. It does not make the Vampire rightful; it makes other minds model the Vampire as the immediate center of danger or command.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Supernatural presence, bloodline authority, command of prey, emotional fixation, and the terrible stillness of something that does not need to breathe.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: The printed body synchronizes chemical cues, subsonic vibration, gaze behavior, vocal harmonics, and identity pressure across biological and synthetic observers.

abilities.name: Predator's Weight
abilities.effect: Cost: none against ordinary mortals; 1 Vitae against supernatural or synthetic minds. Add one die to intimidation or command when you remain still and make your attention unmistakable. The target knows they have been selected. Failure: the target resists but becomes fully aware of your predatory nature.

abilities.name: Command the Pulse
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Vitae. Test: Presence + Command opposed by Resolve + Composure. Issue one immediate, concrete command that can be completed in a few seconds. The target obeys unless the order directly violates a defining conviction or obvious survival. Failure: the target refuses but experiences a visible involuntary reaction that reveals what they feared you would command.

abilities.name: Borrowed Devotion
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Vitae and one minute of focused interaction. Test: Presence + Empathy. Create a temporary fixation, loyalty, aversion, or protective impulse lasting one scene. It colors choices but does not rewrite memory or erase existing bonds. Failure: the emotion takes hold in an unstable form and attaches to the wrong person, symbol, or objective.

abilities.name: Court of One
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Vitae. Your Presence addresses a small group as though every member were receiving personal attention. Make one social test against the highest resistance; each additional resistant target grants them one bonus die. Success imposes one shared emotional posture such as silence, caution, awe, or attention. Failure: the group synchronizes against you instead.

abilities.name: Sovereign Silence
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Vitae and 1 Hunger. For one exchange, suppress panic, argument, unauthorized movement, and hostile initiation within a room or local network. Biological beings feel the presence of an apex predator; compatible machines elevate your identity to emergency priority. Strongly opposed targets may resist at difficulty 4. Afterward, everyone affected remembers the violation clearly unless another power removes it.

powerFamilies.name: Veil of Night
powerFamilies.description: Veil of Night turns concealment into continuity manipulation. The Vampire is not merely unseen; observers and systems are encouraged to classify the Vampire as unimportant, already processed, or belonging to an identity that is not being searched for.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Shadow affinity, forgotten faces, supernatural stealth, altered appearance, and witness memory distorted by predatory magic.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: Skin, scent, thermal output, posture, voice, and noospheric signature coordinate to create a socially and computationally plausible absence.

abilities.name: Unremarked
abilities.effect: Cost: none while calm and nonviolent. Observers do not automatically remember distinguishing details unless they deliberately focus on you. Gain two dice to avoid casual identification, tailing, or retrospective description. Failure: one observer remembers you with unusual clarity and cannot explain why.

abilities.name: Borrowed Face
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Vitae. Alter superficial facial structure, voice, scent, skin temperature, and posture for a scene. The disguise can imitate a known person only with prior observation and does not copy credentials or memories. Failure: the face is convincing to people but contains a biometric inconsistency obvious to careful sensors.

abilities.name: Absent from Record
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Vitae. Test: Guile + Noospherics. Routine cameras, access logs, and identity systems record an incomplete, generic, or already-closed event rather than a useful profile. Success affects one scene or facility segment. Failure: the records are obscured but marked as anomalous, attracting specialist review.

abilities.name: Living Shadow
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Vitae per scene. In dim light, visual clutter, or dense sensor traffic, become a shifting absence that may move through watched areas without presenting a stable target. Attacks made from the effect end it. Failure: you remain concealed from ordinary sight but appear as a distinct void to enhanced or nonvisual senses.

abilities.name: Erase the Witness
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Vitae and 1 Hunger. Test: Guile + Empathy opposed by Resolve + Awareness. Remove, replace, or procedurally close a short recent memory involving you in one target. The edit leaves a seam that contradictory evidence can reopen. Failure: the memory remains, but the target cannot accurately communicate it without experiencing fear or sensory distortion.

powerFamilies.name: Catalytic Flesh
powerFamilies.description: Catalytic Flesh develops the printed organism's imitation of undeath. It controls dormancy, repair, armor, organ redundancy, and the ability to keep a coherent predatory body after injuries that should destroy ordinary life.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Vampiric resilience, corpse-like stillness, unnatural healing, blood-hardened flesh, and the ability to rise from apparently fatal wounds.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: Vitae activates alien repair tissues, mobile organ structures, resinous scaffolds, and metabolic states that resemble death because the body has learned death as a survival procedure.

abilities.name: Cold Repair
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Vitae and one uninterrupted minute. Convert one Trauma into Impact or remove two Impact damage as the body cools, seals vessels, and rebuilds tissue with pale resin. Fire, radiation, and sunlight wounds require two Vitae. Failure: the wound closes but traps contamination or foreign material inside.

abilities.name: Corpse Suspension
abilities.effect: Cost: none to enter; 1 Vitae to awaken instantly. Shut down pulse, respiration, heat, movement, and most detectable metabolism for up to one day per Archetype Rating. You remain dimly aware of touch and severe danger. Failure: none, but awakening without Vitae inflicts 1 Hunger and temporary sensory confusion.

abilities.name: Ossuary Armor
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Vitae. Grow subdermal plates, dense fibers, and reinforced joints for a scene, gaining Armor equal to half Archetype Rating rounded up. The transformation is visibly inhuman at close range. Failure: armor forms unevenly, granting protection but reducing Finesse by one die.

abilities.name: Reassemble the Dead Shape
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Vitae. Reaction after suffering catastrophic injury, dismemberment, or organ destruction. Keep the self-pattern coherent, pull separated tissue toward the body when physically possible, and remain recoverable rather than destroyed. Full restoration requires time and biological material. Failure: survival succeeds, but one replaced organ develops an alien function or appetite.

abilities.name: Sovereign Carcass
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Vitae and 1 Hunger. For one scene, choose to be treated as living, dead, or suspended for biological, medical, environmental, and some supernatural effects. Ignore penalties from ordinary poison, vacuum, pressure, and nonradiant injury, and remain active at zero Vitality. When the scene ends, all deferred damage returns; any amount beyond your maximum becomes permanent Trauma unless you immediately feed or enter dormancy.

powerFamilies.name: Vital Predation
powerFamilies.description: Vital Predation explores what feeding means when blood, nourishment, identity, memory, and biological function can be separated. It allows the Vampire to survive new ecologies while forcing explicit choices about what forms of life they are willing to consume.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Blood drinking, hunting, tasting emotion through Vitae, draining life, and the intimate violence of sustaining undeath through another body.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: Specialized sensory and catalytic organs analyze vital media and eventually extract usable function from alien metabolism, synthetic life, noospheric priority, and continuity-linked energy.

abilities.name: Taste the Current
abilities.effect: Cost: none. By tasting a trace of blood, hemolymph, nutrient fluid, or living tissue, learn whether it can restore Vitae, quiet Hunger, carry disease, contain foreign memory, or provoke mutation. Failure: you identify nutritional value but miss one contaminant or emotional imprint.

abilities.name: Alien Draught
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Hunger gained after feeding. Consume a normally incompatible biological fluid and convert it into Vitae without immediate poisoning. Test Resilience + Medicine to avoid a temporary alien sensory trait, instinct, or visible mutation. Failure: Vitae is restored, but the borrowed trait lasts until the next feeding.

abilities.name: Channel Hunger
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Vitae. Select one nearby wounded, frightened, or metabolically active target you can perceive. For the scene, gain one die to track, intimidate, or resist deception from that target, and reduce one Hunger penalty while pursuing them. Failure: the fixation attaches to the strongest vital source present, including an ally.

abilities.name: Feed on Function
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Vitae to initiate. Drain a narrow vital function from a willing, restrained, or defeated target: body heat, regenerative capacity, sensory acuity, stored metabolic charge, or noospheric processing priority. You gain a related temporary benefit while the target suffers a matching penalty. Failure: the function transfers incompletely and creates a shared symptom between both bodies.

abilities.name: Eclipse Feast
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Vitae and 1 Hunger. During direct contact with a powerful organism, synthetic intelligence, or continuity engine, feed upon the principle sustaining its active identity rather than only its fluid. Restore Vitae to maximum and temporarily borrow one defining resistance or sensory capacity. The target loses access to that quality for one scene. Failure: the feeding succeeds, but a fragment of the target's priorities or memories becomes part of your Hunger until resolved.

powerFamilies.name: Blood Memory
powerFamilies.description: Blood Memory treats lineage as information carried through sensation, instinct, and Vitae. With no sire-chain available to confirm the past, the Vampire can recover, share, challenge, and eventually author what bloodline identity means in the Continuum.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Ancestral blood, sire bonds, inherited disciplines, clan memory, emotional resonance through feeding, and the social authority of lineage.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: Catalytic fluid stores procedural impressions and identity fragments. Feeding, transfusion, and deliberate circulation can move memories between continuations even when the original bloodline metaphysics are absent.

abilities.name: Echo in the Vitae
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Vitae or a fresh sample. Test: Awareness + Empathy. Recover one sensory impression, practiced motion, dominant emotion, or recent fear carried in the sample. The memory is experienced rather than narrated. Failure: you receive a true impression but misidentify whose perspective it represents.

abilities.name: Sireless Communion
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Vitae from each participant. Share a controlled memory, emotion, or learned bodily rhythm with another Vampire or biologically compatible continuation. Both participants know which material was intentionally shared. Failure: one unrelated blood-memory crosses with it.

abilities.name: Inherited Skill
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Vitae and one available blood-memory. For one scene, use a stored procedural memory as a temporary Skill rating of 2 or add two dice to a Skill you already possess. The borrowed competence carries a recognizable mannerism or emotional bias. Failure: the skill functions, but the memory tries to complete an old objective.

abilities.name: Ancestral Court
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Vitae and one hour of dormancy. Convene several stored blood-memory personas as advisory fragments. Ask up to three questions about predation, politics, survival, or supernatural precedent. They answer from their own incomplete experiences and may disagree. Failure: one fragment remains active after the consultation and influences Hunger.

abilities.name: Author the Bloodline
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Vitae, 1 Hunger, and a willing recipient or preserved vessel. Deliberately create a stable bloodline derivative by encoding one power tell, feeding adaptation, ethical prohibition, or inherited memory practice into Vitae. Future recipients can learn it through feeding or transfusion. This does not guarantee obedience or kinship; it makes you responsible for a new lineage tradition that did not exist in the old world.

archetypes.name: Shapechanger
archetypes.theme: A person who was never one body, now reconstructed as several remembered anatomical and spiritual selves compressed into one morphogenic alien organism.
archetypes.weaknessText: High Instinct makes confinement, humiliation, threats to pack, violated territory, and unresolved pursuit increasingly difficult to tolerate. One form may begin claiming to be the only honest self.

innateAbilities.name: Threefold Form
innateAbilities.effect: You possess a human approximation, a hunting configuration, and a war configuration. Shifting costs 1 Fury in danger unless a power states otherwise; outside danger it can be performed slowly without cost.

innateAbilities.name: Living Regeneration
innateAbilities.effect: Recover one Impact at scene end. Spend 1 Fury during a brief pause to recover additional Impact equal to half Archetype Rating, using redundant organs, resinous repair, and tissue redistribution.

innateAbilities.name: Pack Sense
innateAbilities.effect: Recognize the direction and broad emotional condition of a bonded packmate through chemical, vibrational, noospheric, and continuity cues even when their body, species, or appearance changes.

powerFamilies.name: Warform
powerFamilies.description: Warform governs the bodies taken when negotiation ends. It develops from remembered predatory anatomy into deliberate combat architecture built for corridors, zero gravity, hostile atmosphere, armored targets, and enemies no terrestrial predator evolved to fight.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Supernatural war shapes, claws, mass, regeneration, rage, and the terrible honesty of becoming the body meant for direct violence.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: Stored tissue unfolds, organ anchors move, support plates lock, leverage changes, and redundant systems come online under the direction of remembered identity.

abilities.name: Predator's Frame
abilities.effect: Cost: none in hunting form; 1 Fury to activate instantly. Gain enhanced scent, low-light perception, balance, and speed, adding two dice to tracking, pursuit, or close-range ambush. Failure: none, but a strong prey cue can raise Instinct by 1.

abilities.name: Claws of Decision
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Fury. In war form, grow a chosen natural weapon with Cutting, Crushing, Piercing, or Grappling tags. Unarmed attacks inflict Trauma and may damage ordinary armor. Failure: the weapon forms imperfectly, retaining damage but imposing one die of Finesse penalty.

abilities.name: Massive Shift
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Fury and enough physical room. Add Archetype Rating to Force or Resilience for a scene as stored tissue, fluid, and structural plates redeploy. You may smash barriers or carry extraordinary mass, but become difficult to conceal and vulnerable in confined spaces. Failure: the shift succeeds but damages nearby equipment or terrain.

abilities.name: Siege Anatomy
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Fury. Configure the war form against one obstacle class: sealed doors, powered armor, swarms, heavy recoil, radiation, or crushing pressure. Gain armor, reach, anchoring, or a specialized attack appropriate to the choice for one scene. Failure: the anatomy solves the obstacle but sacrifices another capability such as speed, speech, or fine manipulation.

abilities.name: Apex Shape
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Fury and 1 Instinct. Assume a unique apex form designed around one environment and one predatory purpose. Gain armor equal to half Archetype Rating, one extraordinary movement mode, and one severe natural weapon or control adaptation. The form lasts a scene and becomes part of your permanent body-memory, meaning future involuntary transformations may attempt to use it.

powerFamilies.name: Hunt Across Worlds
powerFamilies.description: Hunt Across Worlds turns pursuit into continuity recognition. The Shapechanger learns to follow a target through changed bodies, false identities, environmental transitions, network traces, and reflection spaces rather than relying on ordinary scent alone.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Tracking, prey fixation, scent memory, pursuit, territorial awareness, and the instinct that a chosen quarry remains the same creature wherever it runs.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: The hunting body combines chemical traces, vibration, emotional rhythm, noospheric residue, and discontinuities left by copied or transferred identity.

abilities.name: Scent of Continuity
abilities.effect: Cost: none. Test: Awareness + Survival. After directly sensing a target, recognize their continuation through superficial disguise, altered scent, or ordinary body replacement for the rest of the operation. Failure: you identify the correct identity family but cannot distinguish the current instance from a close copy.

abilities.name: Mark the Prey
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Fury. Choose one target you have personally perceived. Gain one die to track, pursue, defend against, or resist deception from them, and know when they cross the local area's physical boundary. Failure: the mark attaches to something they own, control, or recently touched rather than the target directly.

abilities.name: Impossible Trail
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Fury. Follow a route through sealed environments, vacuum transitions, teleport-like transit, networked identity movement, or copied bodies by interpreting the discontinuity rather than a physical footprint. Test Awareness + Survival, difficulty 3. Failure: you recover the destination category but not the exact location.

abilities.name: Pursuit Through Systems
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Fury and 1 Instinct. Enter hunting focus for a scene. Doors, crowds, automated defenses, and unfamiliar terrain lose two dice when they merely delay you rather than directly defeat you. You may use Survival in place of Systems Intrusion or Xenoculture to follow the quarry's route through infrastructure. Failure: you continue the pursuit but ignore one unrelated danger to the pack.

abilities.name: No Escape Between Selves
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Fury and a preserved trace of the target. Declare the person, process, or predatory identity you are hunting. For one operation, body transfer, duplication, memory editing, disguise, or legal identity change cannot fully break your recognition. You always know which encountered instance carries the strongest continuity with the marked target. The power does not reveal location at unlimited range, and destroying the wrong copy can still have moral consequences.

powerFamilies.name: Pack Continuity
powerFamilies.description: Pack Continuity rebuilds the social and spiritual reality of pack after Q-MAP. It allows individuals with different bodies, origins, and even species to coordinate as one survival organism without erasing their autonomy.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Pack bonds, shared hunting rhythm, hierarchy, mutual protection, howl, scent, kinship, and the certainty that survival is distributed across more than one body.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: Bonded continuations synchronize through vibration, chemical state, emotional cadence, noospheric signature, and repeated acts of recognition.

abilities.name: Pack Pulse
abilities.effect: Cost: none with a bonded ally. Sense whether a packmate is calm, afraid, injured, enraged, unconscious, or under external control within the same local area. Test Awareness + Empathy to distinguish their emotion from your own. Failure: you receive the correct intensity but misread its cause.

abilities.name: Coordinated Instinct
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Fury. Choose up to Archetype Rating packmates in communication range. For one round, each may use your Initiative or add one die to an action directly supporting another member. Failure: coordination succeeds, but all participants briefly share the highest current Instinct or equivalent pressure among them.

abilities.name: Share the Wound
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Fury. Reaction when a bonded ally suffers damage, Disruption, or forced separation. Transfer up to two points of the effect to yourself or divide it among consenting packmates. The transferred condition changes expression according to each body. Failure: the wound is shared, but so is one associated sensory memory or compulsion.

abilities.name: Many Bodies, One Hunt
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Fury. For one scene, bonded packmates may exchange sensory impressions and lend one Attribute die to one another once per round. No member loses their own perspective, but the group can coordinate without speech across darkness, vacuum, or hostile signal conditions. Failure: the link works while one intrusive memory or instinct circulates through everyone.

abilities.name: Pack Is a Territory
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Fury and 1 Instinct. Define the current pack as a mobile domain. While at least two members remain able to act, no member can be isolated by ordinary walls, crowds, signal loss, fear, or false identity without an opposed test against your Force + Resolve. Members always know a viable route toward one another. The effect ends if the pack knowingly abandons one of its members.

powerFamilies.name: Morphogenic Architecture
powerFamilies.description: Morphogenic Architecture treats the printed body as a library of possible anatomy. It is not shapeshifting for disguise alone; it is controlled redesign of organs, mass, interfaces, and survival systems.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Partial transformations, supernatural adaptation, regenerative body control, animal traits, and the instinctive certainty that flesh is negotiable.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: Ar'nock-derived tissues can unfold, dissolve, reprint, and reposition structures in response to remembered forms and environmental demand.

abilities.name: Utility Shift
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Fury or several minutes outside danger. Develop one limited adaptation for a scene: climbing pads, gills, sealable nostrils, vibration whiskers, gripping toes, translucent eyelids, tool-like claws, or similar anatomy. Failure: the adaptation works but remains visible after the scene until you rest.

abilities.name: Borrowed Organ
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Fury and a biological sample or observed function. Grow a temporary organ approximating one nonunique capability such as toxin filtration, pressure sensing, heat exchange, electroreception, or nutrient digestion. Failure: the organ functions but introduces a foreign appetite, reflex, or sensory bias.

abilities.name: Environmental Form
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Fury and one minute of transformation. Configure the whole body for vacuum, deep pressure, toxic atmosphere, microgravity, radiation shielding, extreme cold, or intense heat for one scene. Gain two dice to survival and movement in that environment. Failure: the adaptation is incomplete and requires equipment support to avoid damage.

abilities.name: Rebuild the Template
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Fury and one hour of rest or printer access. Permanently alter one minor bodily feature, remove one persistent physical Complication, or replace one damaged organ with a new design. The change becomes part of every form unless specifically suppressed. Failure: the repair succeeds but creates a new visible irregularity or dependency.

abilities.name: Species of One
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Fury and 1 Instinct. Design a completely new stable form with a defined ecological role, movement method, sensory emphasis, and one extraordinary adaptation. It cannot simply combine every advantage. Once created, the form becomes a permanent identity option and may develop its own instincts, preferences, and claim to authenticity.

powerFamilies.name: Spirit Ecology
powerFamilies.description: Spirit Ecology replaces inherited assumptions about the Umbra or old reflection realms with careful relationships among ship minds, archive ghosts, habitat intelligences, swarms, engineered ecosystems, and nonlocal presences.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Spirit sight, totem pacts, crossing into reflection space, bargaining with place spirits, and recognizing that landscapes possess memory and intention.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: Auxiliary nerves perceive noospheric pressure, ecological feedback, machine habit, emotional residue, and dimensional stress as overlapping forms of presence.

abilities.name: Scent the Unseen
abilities.effect: Cost: none. Test: Awareness + Xenoculture. Detect nearby incorporeal, noospheric, ecological, machine, emotional, or reflection-space presences and learn the broad category of attention they represent. Failure: you detect presence but classify it according to an old-world category that may be dangerously wrong.

abilities.name: Threshold Step
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Fury. Perceive and briefly interact with the nearest reflection or resonance layer without fully leaving the physical body. You may speak, touch one simple object, or observe hidden routes for one exchange. Failure: interaction succeeds, but something on the other side also perceives your physical location.

abilities.name: Totemic Accord
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Fury and a negotiated offering, service, or constraint. Form a temporary pact with a local spirit, machine-presence, archive, habitat intelligence, or ecological regulator. Gain one narrow favor consistent with its nature. Failure: the agreement is valid, but one term is interpreted through local rather than old-world custom.

abilities.name: Walk the Other Side
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Fury. Cross fully into a nearby reflection, resonance, or noospheric environment with willing companions. Physical distance may behave differently there, but local inhabitants and hazards are real. Failure: the crossing succeeds while one carried item, memory, or companion appears in a neighboring layer and must be recovered.

abilities.name: Found a New Totem
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Fury, 1 Instinct, and a sustained relationship with a local presence. Establish a mutual totemic bond between the pack and a machine mind, habitat, ecosystem, archive, or reflection entity. The totem grants one persistent thematic benefit and one binding obligation. It is a participant with needs and agency, not an equipment slot.

powerFamilies.name: Territorial Sovereignty
powerFamilies.description: Territorial Sovereignty turns place into a reciprocal relationship. The Shapechanger does not merely claim ground; they learn its routes, systems, living inhabitants, pressure patterns, and defensive reflexes until the territory recognizes the claim.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Marking territory, defending dens, reading landscape, awakening local spirits, and the instinctive authority of a predator on familiar ground.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: Scent, vibration, noospheric markers, ecological feedback, and physical patrol create a distributed map shared between the Shapechanger and the environment.

abilities.name: Claim the Ground
abilities.effect: Cost: none after ten minutes of exploration. Mark a room, camp, corridor network, or small natural site as temporary territory. Know when a large creature, armed group, or major system change crosses its boundary. Failure: you sense entry but cannot distinguish intruder from environmental movement.

abilities.name: Warning Scent
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Fury. Place a chemical, vibrational, or noospheric warning that allies instinctively recognize and ordinary intruders find unsettling. Allies gain one die to Initiative inside the marked area. Failure: the warning also attracts one local predator, security process, or curious intelligence.

abilities.name: Living Perimeter
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Fury per scene. Link your senses to several points in claimed territory through surfaces, small organisms, sensors, echoes, or spirits. You cannot be casually surprised there and may track movement without direct line of sight. Failure: the perimeter functions, but one point feeds you false information due to damage or hostile influence.

abilities.name: Territory Fights Back
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Fury. Command claimed terrain to hinder intruders through doors, machinery, animals, pressure changes, debris, lights, alarms, or spirit activity. The territory takes one significant environmental action each round for three rounds. Failure: it responds with excessive force or damages something the pack needed intact.

abilities.name: Domain of the Continuum Beast
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Fury, 1 Instinct, and sustained occupation. Transform a major site into a persistent domain recognized by local systems, inhabitants, and reflection layers. The pack gains superior awareness, recovery, and movement there, while hostile powers must contest the domain before rewriting its rules. The territory develops needs of its own and can be wounded, neglected, or politically challenged.

archetypes.name: Eldritch Binder
archetypes.theme: A person carrying the structure of a relationship with the impossible, uncertain whether the original patron, a fragment, an address, an empty wound, or a local replacement now answers.
archetypes.weaknessText: Every use teaches the answering presence more about the body, team, and local universe. High Intrusion creates compulsions, sensory overlap, independent organs, altered terms, or partial manifestations.

innateAbilities.name: Bound Fragment
innateAbilities.effect: Choose the old relationship and what may have crossed: patron, fragment, address, wound, procedural copy, or uncertain successor. The answer can remain unresolved during play.

innateAbilities.name: Name and Boundary
innateAbilities.effect: Given time and enough understanding, establish a ward, invitation condition, or prohibition addressing a correctly identified category of being, process, memory, or action.

innateAbilities.name: Forbidden Comprehension
innateAbilities.effect: Spend 1 Pact to understand the immediate function or intent of an alien symbol, ritual, anomaly, or device without receiving a safe human explanation or complete historical context.

powerFamilies.name: Sealcraft
powerFamilies.description: Sealcraft creates temporary local law. Its strength depends less on decorative geometry than on correctly naming what is being constrained, what action is forbidden, and what boundary the new universe will recognize.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Circles, wards, true names, prohibitions, bindings, ritual containment, and inherited occult rules governing invitation and trespass.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: The printed body produces chemical traces, electromagnetic fields, biological geometry, and noospheric markers that local systems interpret as enforceable categories.

abilities.name: Chalk Boundary
abilities.effect: Cost: none with preparation or 1 Pact instantly. Draw, secrete, project, or declare a boundary against one named lesser category such as hostile spirit, unauthorized drone, copied memory, predatory organism, or open flame. Crossing requires a successful resistance test. Failure: the boundary works on the category as worded, exposing any mistake in your definition.

abilities.name: Closed Mouth
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Pact. Test: Resolve + Noospherics opposed by Resolve + Composure. Prevent one target from speaking, transmitting, invoking, or deliberately writing a chosen name, command phrase, secret, or activation sequence for a scene. Failure: the prohibition affects direct expression but not metaphor, gesture, or proxy action.

abilities.name: Anchor the Impossible
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Pact. Fix one portal, projection, manifestation, unstable object, copied identity, or shifting spatial relationship into its current state for up to Archetype Rating rounds. The target may resist. Failure: the state is anchored, but so is one associated hazard or occupant.

abilities.name: Prison of Meaning
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Pact and a prepared vessel. Bind an incorporeal, informational, mnemonic, or noospheric entity into an object, body compartment, isolated process, or symbol that meaningfully represents it. The prison must be maintained by a clear rule. Failure: containment succeeds but the vessel acquires one ability or compulsion from the prisoner.

abilities.name: Law of the Room
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Pact and 1 Intrusion. State one clear supernatural rule governing a contained area for a scene: no one may cross without invitation, spoken lies become visible, copied minds cannot merge, weapons cannot discharge, or a similarly bounded law. Powerful targets may contest it. The law applies to you as written, and ambiguous wording is interpreted by the answering presence rather than by your intent.

powerFamilies.name: Borrowed Anatomy
powerFamilies.description: Borrowed Anatomy gives physical support to capacities that were once purely metaphysical. The Binder's body becomes an experimental embassy, growing organs and structures modeled on the needs of an intelligence that may never have possessed compatible flesh.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Impossible senses, patron-granted limbs, inhuman movement, temporary possession, protective manifestations, and bodily signs of the pact.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: Ar'nock tissues respond to symbolic instruction, growing glands, sensory organs, cavities, armor, and locomotor structures from memories that were never originally biological.

abilities.name: Other Eye
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Pact. Manifest a temporary organ able to perceive one hidden quality: heat, resonance, dimensional stress, memory residue, noospheric attention, active lies, or biological incompatibility. It lasts a scene. Failure: the organ works but cannot close itself until you rest.

abilities.name: Hand Through the Gap
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Pact. Reach through a short impossible angle to touch, manipulate, or retrieve something nearby but physically obstructed. The route cannot pass through a fully sealed supernatural boundary. Failure: contact succeeds, but the hand emerges from a point visible to an unwanted observer.

abilities.name: Mantle of the Guest
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Pact and 1 Intrusion if maintained beyond one scene. Grow protective anatomy reflecting the presence's nature: mirrored plates, jointless skin, orbiting eyes, articulated shadow, pressure-resistant shell, or similar form. Gain Armor equal to half Archetype Rating and one thematic resistance. Failure: the mantle grants protection while altering voice, appetite, or behavior.

abilities.name: Unnatural Locomotion
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Pact. For one scene, move according to an anatomy that ignores one ordinary limitation: cling to any surface, fold through narrow spaces, step across gaps, swim through dense machinery, or move while physically inverted. Failure: movement works, but the body retains the wrong orientation or joint arrangement afterward.

abilities.name: Body of the Embassy
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Pact and 1 Intrusion. Transform into a stable hybrid body capable of hosting a controlled portion of the presence without surrendering agency. Gain two chosen borrowed organs, one extraordinary sense, and one major resistance for a scene. The presence may speak through you but cannot act independently unless you violate a negotiated boundary. Failure is replaced by consequence: one new organ remains permanently and develops needs.

powerFamilies.name: Pact Economy
powerFamilies.description: Pact Economy treats favors, obligations, prohibitions, payment, and consent as manipulable occult structure. It is powerful because the Binder understands that even impossible beings require terms by which action becomes legitimate.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Bargains, geasa, offerings, inherited debts, ritual payment, names exchanged for services, and the danger of asking for power without specifying cost.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: Obligations can attach to copied identities, machine citizens, autonomous processes, habitats, and continuity records as well as souls or spirits.

abilities.name: Name the Price
abilities.effect: Cost: none. Before accepting a supernatural, noospheric, or institutional bargain, ask what the other party actually gains, what obligation will remain afterward, and what unstated resource is being risked. The Game Moderator must answer each in broad but truthful terms. Failure: none, though the answer may reveal that the cost is emotional, political, or delayed.

abilities.name: Deferred Payment
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Pact. Delay one immediate cost, backlash, pressure increase, or demanded offering from a power or agreement until the end of the scene. The debt remains exact and cannot be forgotten. Failure: the payment is delayed, but interest adds a narrow additional obligation.

abilities.name: Transfer Obligation
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Pact and genuine consent from the recipient, unless the original contract permits assignment. Move a supernatural duty, ward maintenance, service, or payment from one valid party to another. Failure: the transfer works only partially, making both parties responsible.

abilities.name: Renegotiate the Impossible
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Pact. Test: Resolve + Negotiation opposed by the other party's authority. Reopen one existing pact term because circumstances, identity, universe, or body have materially changed. Exchange one obligation, prohibition, or reward for another of comparable weight. Failure: negotiations reveal a loophole the other party may use before talks resume.

abilities.name: Sovereign Contract
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Pact and 1 Intrusion. Draft a binding agreement among willing biological, synthetic, spiritual, or institutional parties. Each clause must define action, duration, consideration, and exit. Violations become immediately perceptible and trigger a predeclared consequence no stronger than the benefit received. The agreement cannot manufacture consent; coercion creates a flaw that can eventually void the whole structure.

powerFamilies.name: Forbidden Cognition
powerFamilies.description: Forbidden Cognition allows the Binder to borrow a nonhuman mode of understanding without pretending it is safe, complete, or objective. Knowledge arrives as altered perception, impossible comparison, and memories that may not belong to the current universe.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Occult revelation, patron whispers, impossible languages, prophetic dreams, symbolic interpretation, and truths that damage the mind because human categories cannot contain them.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: The printed nervous system creates temporary cognitive organs and pathways capable of parsing alien intention, causal structure, and nonlocal relationships.

abilities.name: Read the Wound
abilities.effect: Cost: none once per scene. Examine an anomaly, possession, broken pact, impossible device, or corrupted space and identify whether it was opened, invited, forced, inherited, copied, or grown. Failure: you identify the mechanism but briefly feel the event from the intruding side.

abilities.name: Impossible Translation
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Pact. Understand the immediate operational meaning of an alien language, ritual notation, machine prayer, biological display, or nonverbal warning for a scene. You do not gain cultural mastery. Failure: the translation is literal but misses irony, taboo, legal status, or emotional context.

abilities.name: Ask the Passenger
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Pact and 1 Intrusion. Ask the answering presence one direct question within its demonstrated domain. It must provide a useful response but may answer through image, compulsion, analogy, or sensory transformation. Failure: the answer is still useful, but the presence learns one personal fact you intended to keep private.

abilities.name: Remember What Never Happened
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Pact. Access one plausible unrealized memory connected to the current situation: a route not taken, a failed ritual, a version of the scene where someone made another choice. Gain two dice on one action using the lesson. Failure: the memory is useful but emotionally indistinguishable from lived experience.

abilities.name: Library Behind the Eyes
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Pact and 1 Intrusion. For one scene, become a controlled access point to the presence's accumulated categories and memories. Treat Reason as 5 for understanding anomalies, alien systems, pacts, and nonlocal entities, and ask up to three clarifying questions. Afterward, choose one human memory that becomes temporarily inaccessible until you rest and re-anchor it.

powerFamilies.name: Threshold Geometry
powerFamilies.description: Threshold Geometry manipulates the relationship between here and there. It is not unrestricted teleportation; it creates routes by exploiting boundaries, conceptual adjacency, reflection layers, and the fact that some spaces are closer in meaning than in distance.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Summoning circles, hidden doors, impossible angles, dream passage, ritual crossroads, and places where the world is thin.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: The Binder combines spatial discontinuities, noospheric topology, biological growth, and symbolic correspondence to create temporary traversable relationships.

abilities.name: Folded Reach
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Pact. Treat one nearby surface, opening, or reflected image as adjacent to another point within several meters for the purpose of sight, hearing, or touch. Failure: the connection works one way only.

abilities.name: Angle Without Distance
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Pact. Step around an impossible angle and emerge at another visible point in the same room or connected corridor. You must cross a real threshold such as a doorway, shadow line, hatch rim, or reflected edge. Failure: you arrive correctly but leave an afterimage or echo that persists.

abilities.name: Door in the Wrong Wall
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Pact and one minute of preparation. Create a temporary passage through one barrier by defining it as a boundary rather than an object. The route cannot bypass a stronger active seal. Failure: the door opens, but it exits into the nearest semantically related space rather than the intended one.

abilities.name: Transit the Unmade Route
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Pact. Move yourself and willing companions through a reflection, noospheric, dreamlike, or causal route to a location you can meaningfully identify within the same site. The passage exposes travelers to one local hazard or resident. Failure: the group arrives separated across adjacent destinations.

abilities.name: Cartography of Elsewhere
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Pact and 1 Intrusion. Map a persistent nonordinary route connecting two established thresholds across a major distance. The route has conditions of entry, inhabitants, and a maintenance requirement chosen during creation. It cannot be used casually by those who do not understand its rule, but every crossing teaches the answering presence more about both endpoints.

powerFamilies.name: Invocation
powerFamilies.description: Invocation determines how much of the answering presence may enter local reality and under whose terms. It moves from recognizable signs to negotiated audience without assuming that greater manifestation means greater control.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Calling signs, possession, patron avatars, summoned servants, divine or demonic audience, and the terrible escalation from borrowing power to allowing presence.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: The body, environment, networks, and reflection layers provide progressively larger interfaces through which the presence can express itself.

abilities.name: Whispered Sign
abilities.effect: Cost: none. Produce a small unmistakable sign associated with the presence: altered gravity, impossible shadow, repeated symbol, localized silence, unusual biological response, or machine behavior. Gain one die to prove connection or intimidate those who understand it. Failure: the sign appears somewhere nearby rather than where intended.

abilities.name: Borrowed Presence
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Pact. Allow the presence to speak, see, or sense through one organ, object, or device for a minute. You choose the channel and may end it. Failure: the presence uses an additional nearby channel before withdrawing.

abilities.name: Local Avatar
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Pact and 1 Intrusion. Create a temporary limited avatar from shadow, tissue, machinery, memory, or environmental material. It performs one defined task using a pool equal to Archetype Rating + 2 and cannot exceed the agreed scope. Failure: the avatar completes the task according to literal wording rather than intention.

abilities.name: Partial Arrival
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Pact and 1 Intrusion. Manifest a major portion of the presence through your body or a prepared site, producing one large effect consistent with its nature: break a seal, silence a network, hold a breach, terrify a crowd, or alter local geometry. You retain veto over one action. Failure: the effect succeeds, but the presence chooses its own visible form and message.

abilities.name: Full Audience
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Pact, 2 Intrusion, and a prepared boundary. Bring the answering presence into a stable negotiated audience for one scene without granting unrestricted embodiment. It may converse, bargain, perceive the area, and perform one agreed act. All participants can determine that something real is present, but not whether it is the original patron. Ending the audience safely requires honoring the dismissal terms established at the beginning.

archetypes.name: Harmonic Mutant
archetypes.theme: A body already rewritten by frequency, now amplified by Ar'nock biology until flesh, matter, emotion, memory, and ship systems can enter the same dangerous arrangement.
archetypes.weaknessText: Opposing frequencies, emotional shock, environmental coupling, and repeated power use increase Discord. The ship or nearby bodies may reinforce a pattern you did not intend to sustain.

innateAbilities.name: Living Frequency
innateAbilities.effect: Sense strong vibration, structural stress, active fields, biological rhythm, and emotional resonance through dedicated printed organs.

innateAbilities.name: Adaptive Tissue
innateAbilities.effect: Choose one persistent mutation such as vibration sense, pressure tolerance, resinous healing, phase-flexible joints, luminous communication, or conductive skin.

innateAbilities.name: Tune the Self
innateAbilities.effect: Spend 1 Resonance to alter one bodily parameter for a scene: density, elasticity, thermal behavior, electrical resistance, pressure tolerance, or sensory range.

powerFamilies.name: Harmonic Projection
powerFamilies.description: Harmonic Projection emits force, disruption, protection, and large-scale tuning through controlled resonance. It is the Mutant's most direct family, but every projected note can couple to unintended structures or emotions.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Sonic attacks, vibration control, resonance shields, destructive frequency, and the ability to hear the hidden note of matter.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: Specialized organs generate pressure, electromagnetic, chemical, and structural oscillations across several ranges simultaneously.

abilities.name: Resonant Tap
abilities.effect: Cost: none. Test: Awareness + Science. Read the broad composition, hollowness, stress, active vibration, or recent impact history of a touched object or surface. Failure: the reading is accurate but overwhelms one ordinary sense for an exchange.

abilities.name: Shatter Note
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Resonance. Test: Composure + Science or Ranged attack. Emit a focused pulse that fractures brittle material, disrupts a lock, staggers a target, or interrupts a delicate mechanism. Failure: the target is affected, but the frequency propagates into one adjacent object or ally's equipment.

abilities.name: Frequency Armor
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Resonance per scene. Surround yourself or a nearby ally with a tuned field that reduces the first physical damage suffered each round by Archetype Rating. It is most effective against repeated force profiles. Failure: protection works, but the field amplifies one unfamiliar damage type.

abilities.name: Catastrophic Chord
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Resonance. Choose a bounded target such as a wall, engine, formation, or hostile field. Build a three-note sequence over one round; on release, inflict major structural damage, silence active vibration, or force the target out of resonance with its support system. Failure: the chord works but produces a dangerous harmonic in the surrounding area.

abilities.name: Living Catastrophe
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Resonance and 1 Discord. Release a controlled wave across a large scene. Choose rupture, absolute silence, mass disorientation, structural stabilization, or synchronized shutdown. The effect changes the environment rather than targeting individuals one at a time. Afterward, your body continues emitting a weaker version of the chosen state until you are deliberately retuned.

powerFamilies.name: Echo Biology
powerFamilies.description: Echo Biology treats organisms as repeatable rhythms. It heals, copies, links, and multiplies living patterns while risking transferred wounds, foreign emotions, and echo bodies that experience themselves as real.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Sympathetic healing, body resonance, adaptive mutation, sensory doubles, shared pain, and biological synchronization.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: Distributed tissues record temporary body patterns and transmit them through touch, vibration, atmosphere, and shared fields.

abilities.name: Sympathetic Healing
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Resonance and one minute of contact. Match another living body's rhythm and convert one Trauma into Impact or remove two Impact. You experience a brief sensory echo of the injury. Failure: healing occurs, but you copy one symptom or pain response for the scene.

abilities.name: Echo Double
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Resonance. Create a short-lived sensory and kinetic afterimage that repeats your most recent movement. It can draw fire, trigger a simple sensor, or provide one die to defense. Failure: the double repeats an emotionally significant earlier action instead of the intended motion.

abilities.name: Shared Frequency
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Resonance per scene. Link willing allies so they can communicate through vibration, sense distress, and lend one die to Medicine, Athletics, or Composure tests involving another linked member. Failure: the link works, but the strongest pain or fear is shared by everyone.

abilities.name: Rewrite the Scar
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Resonance and one hour of tuning. Permanently alter a minor body trait, remove one persistent injury Complication, or convert an old scar into a useful sensory or protective adaptation. Failure: the rewrite succeeds while attaching an emotional memory to the changed tissue.

abilities.name: Chorus Body
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Resonance and 1 Discord. Split into several short-lived physical echo bodies sharing one mind and resource pool. Each echo can act with reduced dice, occupy space, and experience events independently. Recombining integrates all memories; each destroyed echo inflicts 1 Discord and leaves a permanent disagreement about which body was the original.

powerFamilies.name: Structural Resonance
powerFamilies.description: Structural Resonance makes the Mutant an interpreter and participant in architecture. It reads load, redirects stress, wakes biological machinery, and eventually becomes part of the structure carrying everyone else.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Vibration sensing, engineering intuition, seismic awareness, resonance damping, and the ability to hear when a building or machine is about to fail.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: Ar'nock systems treat harmonic feedback as ordinary maintenance, allowing the Mutant to interact with hull, conduits, living walls, and fabrication structures as though sharing a nervous system.

abilities.name: Hullsense
abilities.effect: Cost: none while touching a structure. Learn its nearby cavities, load-bearing paths, active conduits, major damage, and moving masses. Failure: the map is correct but includes one old or phantom layout stored in the material.

abilities.name: Stress Redirection
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Resonance. Reaction when a structure, vehicle, shield, or piece of cover would fail. Move the stress into another connected section, delaying collapse for Archetype Rating rounds. Failure: failure is delayed, but the new stress point becomes more severe.

abilities.name: Living Brace
abilities.effect: Cost: 1 Resonance. Integrate your body with a damaged wall, machine, bridge, pressure seal, or biological structure. Add Composure + Resilience to its effective durability and keep it functional while you remain connected. Failure: the support works, but damage to the structure transfers to you as Impact.

abilities.name: Wake the Architecture
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Resonance. Communicate a simple operational intention to a dormant or damaged Ar'nock system through harmonic activation. Doors, conduits, life support, growth chambers, or repair tissue may perform one native function without normal credentials. Failure: the system awakens in maintenance or defense mode rather than the requested mode.

abilities.name: Become the Load Path
abilities.effect: Cost: 2 Resonance and 1 Discord. For one scene, treat a vehicle, habitat section, large machine, or living structure as an extension of your body. Sense throughout it, redistribute damage, and coordinate its moving parts using your own actions. Damage and emotional shock can flow both ways, and separation at scene end leaves you temporarily uncertain where your body stops.

powerFamilies.name: Emotional Chord
powerFamilies.description: Emotional Chord hears and alters the rhythms by which minds influence one another. It does not manufacture precise beliefs; it tunes intensity, synchronization, and the emotional atmosphere through which decisions become possible.
powerFamilies.oldWorldRoot: Empathic resonance, song, crowd emotion, calming frequency, shared panic, and the way a room's mood can become physically palpable.
powerFamilies.continuumTranslation: The Mutant senses emotional states through voice, posture, chemical exchange, heartbeat, noospheric repetition, and structural vibration, then introduces stabilizing or disruptive counter-rhythms.

abilities.name: Hear the Mood
